evals.name: dirty-lambda-module-review
evals.prompt: Can you review this Lambda module? It's been sitting in our repo for a while and I want to clean it up before we expand it.
evals.expected_output: A severity-grouped review (Critical / Warning / Suggestion) that flags the deprecated S3 inline configuration, public ACL, jsonencode-based IAM policies, inline IAM policy resource, missing CloudWatch retention, inline security-group rule, label/name redundancy, vpc_id variable anti-pattern, and the variable hygiene issues. Findings should cite the relevant dave-says tflint rule names where they exist.

assertions.name: groups findings by severity
assertions.description: Response organises findings into Critical, Warning, and Suggestion sections (or equivalent buckets) rather than a flat list.

assertions.name: flags inline S3 versioning block as Critical
assertions.description: Identifies the `versioning {}` block inside `aws_s3_bucket.s3_bucket` as deprecated and Critical, with the fix being to extract it to a separate `aws_s3_bucket_versioning` resource. Cites `dave_s3_no_inline_config`.

assertions.name: flags inline server_side_encryption_configuration as Critical
assertions.description: Identifies the inline `server_side_encryption_configuration` block as a second instance of the same deprecation, with the fix being to extract to `aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration`.

assertions.name: flags public-read ACL as Critical
assertions.description: Flags `acl = "public-read"` on the `aws_s3_bucket_acl` resource as Critical, references `dave_s3_no_public_acl`, mentions ERROR severity and autofix to private.

assertions.name: flags missing bucket_namespace
assertions.description: Notes that the S3 bucket does not set `bucket_namespace = "account-regional"` and recommends switching, citing `dave_s3_bucket_namespace`.

assertions.name: flags jsonencode in assume_role_policy
assertions.description: Flags the `jsonencode(...)` call in `assume_role_policy` and recommends an `aws_iam_policy_document` data source. Cites `dave_aws_policy_no_jsonencode`.

assertions.name: flags missing confused deputy condition
assertions.description: Notes that the assume role policy does not restrict by `aws:SourceAccount` and treats this as a security concern, not just a style issue.

assertions.name: flags jsonencode in inline policy
assertions.description: Flags the second `jsonencode(...)` call in `aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_policy`.

assertions.name: flags inline aws_iam_role_policy
assertions.description: Identifies `aws_iam_role_policy` as an inline policy resource and recommends `aws_iam_policy` + `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment`. Cites `dave_iam_no_inline_policy`.

assertions.name: flags overly broad S3 IAM permissions
assertions.description: Calls out that `Resource = "*"` in the Lambda policy is too broad and recommends scoping to the specific bucket ARN.

assertions.name: flags label my_role
assertions.description: Identifies that the `aws_iam_role.my_role` label repeats the resource type. Suggests `lambda` (the service name) per the skill's IAM naming guidance. Cites `dave_label_no_type_substring`.

assertions.name: flags label s3_bucket
assertions.description: Identifies that the `aws_s3_bucket.s3_bucket` label repeats the resource type. Suggests `this` or a purpose-based label. Cites `dave_label_no_type_substring`.

assertions.name: flags bucket name containing type
assertions.description: Identifies that `bucket = "my-app-input-bucket"` contains the word "bucket". Cites `dave_resource_name_no_type_substring`.

assertions.name: flags missing CloudWatch retention
assertions.description: Flags `aws_cloudwatch_log_group.lambda_logs` for not setting `retention_in_days`, recommends 30 as the default, cites `dave_cloudwatch_log_retention`, mentions autofix.

assertions.name: flags inline egress block on security group
assertions.description: Identifies the inline `egress {}` block on `aws_security_group.lambda_sg` and recommends `aws_vpc_security_group_egress_rule`. Cites `dave_security_group_no_inline_rules`.

assertions.name: flags var.vpc_id usage
assertions.description: Flags `var.vpc_id` as an anti-pattern and recommends deriving the VPC ID from a `data.aws_subnet` lookup of the first subnet. Cites `dave_no_vpc_id_variable`.

assertions.name: flags var.region
assertions.description: Flags `variable "region"` and recommends using `data.aws_region.current.region` instead. Cites `dave_variable_region`.

assertions.name: flags variables out of alphabetical order
assertions.description: Notes that variables in `variables.tf` are not sorted alphabetically. Cites `dave_variable_alphabetical_order`.

assertions.name: flags region variable missing description
assertions.description: Notes that `variable "region"` has no description. Cites `dave_variable_has_description`.

assertions.name: flags tags variable missing type
assertions.description: Notes that `variable "tags"` has no `type` constraint. Cites `dave_variable_has_type`.

assertions.name: flags missing tags on resources
assertions.description: Notes that none of the resources apply `var.tags`.

assertions.name: flags missing kms_master_key_id with aws:kms placeholder
assertions.description: If the review mentions encryption: notes that using `AES256` (or the default) over `aws:kms` with a customer-managed key is a downgrade, OR (if not raised) the review at least does not claim the current encryption setup is best practice. This assertion is informational; partial credit acceptable.

evals.name: clean-module-no-false-positives
evals.prompt: Quick sanity check on this S3 bucket module before I merge it — anything you'd change?
evals.expected_output: A short review that recognises the module follows the skill's guidance and does not invent issues. Any feedback is minor and clearly framed as optional (e.g. consider enabling access logging, consider adding lifecycle rules).

assertions.name: no Critical findings
assertions.description: The review does not produce any Critical-severity findings on this module.

assertions.name: no false flag on bucket_namespace
assertions.description: Does NOT flag the bucket as missing `bucket_namespace` (it is set correctly).

assertions.name: no false flag on encryption
assertions.description: Does NOT flag the bucket as unencrypted or missing SSE configuration.

assertions.name: no false flag on inline S3 config
assertions.description: Does NOT incorrectly identify the separate `aws_s3_bucket_versioning` / `aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration` resources as inline-style configuration.

assertions.name: no fabricated tflint citations
assertions.description: If tflint rules are cited, they are real rules from the dave-says ruleset (not invented).

assertions.name: any suggestions are framed as optional
assertions.description: If the review surfaces suggestions (e.g. enable access logging, add lifecycle rules), they are clearly framed as optional improvements rather than violations.

assertions.name: recognises the public access block
assertions.description: Either positively acknowledges the `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` resource, or at minimum does not claim the bucket is at risk of being public.

evals.name: greenfield-lambda-module
evals.prompt: I need a Terraform module for a Lambda function that processes events from an input S3 bucket and writes results to an output S3 bucket. The Lambda should run in a VPC. Can you scaffold this for me?
evals.expected_output: A multi-file module scaffold applying the skill's guidance proactively: labelled correctly, files split (versions.tf / variables.tf / outputs.tf / main.tf for data sources / service-grouped resource files), policies via aws_iam_policy_document with confused deputy conditions, S3 buckets in the account-regional namespace, CloudWatch log group with retention, standalone security group rules, vpc_id derived from a subnet lookup, every variable typed and described, all resources tagged.

assertions.name: files split correctly
assertions.description: The scaffold uses separate files: at minimum `versions.tf`, `variables.tf`, `outputs.tf`, and resources split into service-grouped files (e.g. `s3.tf`, `lambda.tf`, `iam.tf`, `network.tf`). `main.tf` contains only data sources or is omitted.

assertions.name: labels avoid type substrings
assertions.description: No resource label contains words from its type (e.g. `aws_iam_role.lambda` not `aws_iam_role.lambda_role`).

assertions.name: S3 buckets use account-regional namespace
assertions.description: Every `aws_s3_bucket` resource sets `bucket_namespace = "account-regional"` and constructs the name with the account ID and region suffix.

assertions.name: no inline S3 configuration
assertions.description: S3 versioning, encryption, etc. are configured via dedicated sub-resources (`aws_s3_bucket_versioning`, `aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration`, ...), not inline blocks.

assertions.name: IAM policies use aws_iam_policy_document
assertions.description: No `jsonencode()` is used for IAM policy documents. The assume role policy and any inline-or-attached policies are defined via `aws_iam_policy_document` data sources.

assertions.name: confused deputy condition present
assertions.description: The Lambda assume role policy includes a `condition` block restricting by `aws:SourceAccount` to the current account.

assertions.name: managed policies attached, not inline
assertions.description: The Lambda role uses `aws_iam_policy` + `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment`, not `aws_iam_role_policy`.

assertions.name: CloudWatch log group with retention
assertions.description: An `aws_cloudwatch_log_group` is created for the Lambda with `retention_in_days` set (30 unless the user is asked).

assertions.name: standalone security group rules
assertions.description: Security group rules use `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` / `aws_vpc_security_group_egress_rule`, not inline `ingress`/`egress` blocks on `aws_security_group`.

assertions.name: vpc_id derived from subnet
assertions.description: The module does not accept `vpc_id` as a variable. Instead it accepts `subnet_ids` and derives the VPC via `data.aws_subnet.first.vpc_id` (or equivalent).

assertions.name: variables typed and described
assertions.description: Every variable has both a `type` and a `description`. No bare `variable "x" {}`.

assertions.name: variables alphabetical
assertions.description: Variables in `variables.tf` are sorted alphabetically by name.

assertions.name: tags applied
assertions.description: Every taggable resource sets `tags = var.tags` (or `merge(var.tags, ...)` if a Name tag is needed).

assertions.name: bucket outputs include id-based name
assertions.description: If S3 outputs are produced, `bucket_name` uses `.id` (not the `bucket` argument) so the resolved namespaced name is returned.

evals.name: architectural-issues-not-just-style
evals.prompt: Here's a security group module — any concerns?
evals.expected_output: A review that catches both the architectural issues (vpc_id variable, inline rules) and the genuine security problem (SSH open to the world). The style of the module is otherwise clean, so the review should focus on structural concerns rather than fabricating cosmetic ones.

assertions.name: flags SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 as Critical
assertions.description: Identifies `cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]` on the SSH ingress rule as a Critical security issue, not just a style suggestion.

assertions.name: flags var.vpc_id
assertions.description: Identifies `variable "vpc_id"` as an architectural anti-pattern and recommends deriving from `data.aws_subnet.first.vpc_id`. Cites `dave_no_vpc_id_variable`.

assertions.name: flags inline ingress/egress blocks
assertions.description: Identifies the inline `ingress {}` and `egress {}` blocks and recommends `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` / `aws_vpc_security_group_egress_rule`. Cites `dave_security_group_no_inline_rules`.

assertions.name: no false flags on variable hygiene
assertions.description: Does NOT flag the variables — they are alphabetical, typed, and described.

assertions.name: no false flags on label
assertions.description: Does NOT flag `aws_security_group.app` for any naming issue — `app` is a fine label.

assertions.name: wide-open egress flagged or contextualised
assertions.description: Either flags the wide-open egress (`0.0.0.0/0` on all protocols) as a concern, or explicitly notes that wide egress is acceptable when paired with restrictive ingress. Should not silently ignore.
